subject: Language Learning
objective: Help a learner infer the meaning and connotation of the word 'meticulous' from three short contexts.
expectedBehavior: Contrast connotation with a near synonym
misconceptions: A dictionary gloss is always sufficient
More animation means better learning
requiredInteraction: Choose or write a sentence using the word.
correctnessCriteria: Connotation is not reduced to a single synonym

subject: Mathematics
objective: Show why assuming the negation can expose a contradiction in a short proof.
misconceptions: Proof by contradiction proves an example
A contradiction is a calculation error
requiredInteraction: Reorder proof steps or reveal the contradiction.

subject: Computer Science
objective: Compare n, n log n and n² growth and explain why constants are secondary asymptotically.
learner: Can read functions and small tables.
expectedBehavior: Ordering becomes clear at large n
Constants are distinguished from growth rate
misconceptions: Big-O is runtime in seconds
A larger constant always dominates
requiredInteraction: Change n or a constant multiplier.
correctnessCriteria: Constants do not change the class
accessibility: chart alt; keyboard; color not sole signal

subject: Biology
objective: Connect light, water and CO2 inputs to glucose and oxygen outputs in a plant cell.
misconceptions: Plants get mass mainly from soil
Photosynthesis is the reverse of breathing in every detail
requiredInteraction: Change light availability or inspect a stage.
correctnessCriteria: Light is not a material input
No claim that plants do not respire

subject: Economics
objective: Show a leftward supply shift raising equilibrium price and lowering quantity.
misconceptions: A supply shock is a movement along supply
Price always rises for demand shifts
correctnessCriteria: Supply shift changes equilibrium as expected

subject: Statistics
objective: Show how mean and standard deviation move a normal density without changing its total area.
expectedBehavior: Density remains a shape, not probability at a point
misconceptions: Probability at a point equals density
Larger standard deviation means larger area

subject: Physics
objective: Show equal and opposite forces on two interacting objects and why they do not cancel because they act on different bodies.
expectedBehavior: Two force arrows on two bodies
Net force per body is shown separately
misconceptions: Action/reaction cancel because equal and opposite
The larger object exerts a larger force
requiredInteraction: Change masses or inspect each free-body diagram.

subject: Chemistry
objective: Connect a molecular structure to the properties contributed by an alcohol, ketone or carboxylic acid group.
misconceptions: All oxygen-containing groups behave the same
A functional group is the whole molecule
requiredInteraction: Switch functional group or inspect a property comparison.

subject: Computer Science
objective: Show why an inner join returns only matching key pairs and how unmatched rows disappear.
misconceptions: JOIN is just stacking tables
INNER JOIN keeps all rows
requiredInteraction: Choose a key or inspect a pair.
correctnessCriteria: Output rows are exactly matching pairs

subject: Literature
objective: Help a learner hear and mark iambic pentameter in a line.
learner: Can clap a rhythm but has not named feet.
misconceptions: Every line with ten syllables is iambic pentameter
Meter is the same as rhyme
requiredInteraction: Mark syllables or compare two lines.
correctnessCriteria: No claim that meter determines quality
accessibility: audio alternative; text-only fallback strongly preferred
